rules: Never reference an asset that does not exist.
Never overwrite a verified scene without a reason.
All scenes must be exactly 5 seconds and 150 frames.
The final video must contain exactly 1800 frames.
All generated visuals must be original or properly licensed.
Do not use copyrighted movie footage or music.
Do not present AI-generated imagery as authentic historical evidence.
Preserve the factual meaning of the approved narration.
Do not use Higgsfield, or any external image- or video-generation service, anywhere in this project.
All visuals are rendered locally in code at native 1080x1920, 30 fps.
ElevenLabs is used only for voiceover narration. It is never used for images, video or transcription.

script.title: WHO'S REALLY CONTROLLING YOUR MIND?
script.narration_delivery: Deep, calm, intriguing male British voice. Controlled pacing, conversational but suspenseful.
script._note: APPROVED SCRIPT, copied verbatim (typographic apostrophes/quotes normalised to straight ones; the words are unchanged). Scene n owns the window [(n-1)*5, n*5] s = 150 frames. `caption_groups` (<=7 words each) and `highlight` are production choices, marked proposed until you approve them per scene; S01's are approved.

scenes.title: THE HOOK
scenes.narration: Your mind has weaknesses you probably don't even know about.
caption_groups: you probably don't even know about.

scenes.title: SOCIAL EXCLUSION
scenes.narration: First, social exclusion: being ignored can threaten our sense of belonging.

scenes.title: THE EMOTIONAL EFFECT
scenes.narration: That feeling can hurt, even when no one says a word.
caption_groups: even when no one says a word.

scenes.title: MIRRORING
scenes.narration: Next, mirroring: people often unconsciously copy gestures and expressions.

scenes.title: THE CHAMELEON EFFECT
scenes.narration: This Chameleon Effect can help interactions feel more natural.

scenes.title: SCARCITY
scenes.narration: Then there's scarcity: limited availability can make things seem more desirable.

scenes.title: URGENCY
scenes.narration: That's why countdowns and 'only a few left' can influence decisions.

scenes.title: FOOT-IN-THE-DOOR
scenes.narration: The foot-in-the-door effect starts with a small request.

scenes.title: SMALL AGREEMENTS
scenes.narration: Agreeing once can make a larger request easier to accept.

scenes.title: PSYCHOLOGICAL REACTANCE
scenes.narration: But threaten someone's freedom, and reactance may make them push back.
caption_groups: and reactance may make them push back.

scenes.title: THE REVELATION
scenes.narration: Sometimes, controlling your choices starts by making you feel you have none.
scenes.delivery: Slow, serious, thought-provoking. Pause slightly before "you have none".

scenes.title: THE REELSTER OUTRO
scenes.delivery: No voiceover. Let the music and visual branding finish the video.
